brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;half-n (level 0) with piece:0,0,1;half-n stacked on it (level 1). I used half bases because the drawer only fits on a half base's cut face, and only the same kind of base can stack on top of it.
bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-half-n-full-div3 on the top storey. It's one bin split into 3 compartments, because each cell takes only one bin.
drawer:0#0,0#cut in the cut face of the bottom half base.
capOpenFaces added 6 caps across both storeys. Afterwards find_sockets offered no more cap places. lockJoints also ran (house rule).

finish.summary: I built a two-storey workbench organizer from North-half hex bases. The top storey holds a full-depth bin split into 3 compartments. The bottom storey has a drawer in its cut face. Every open edge is capped and the joints are bolted. check_build found no rule issues and the mesh-collision check came back clear. I put a pen, a marker and a paint brush standing in the 3 compartments to show what it's for. I tried a screwdriver and a hex driver first, but they wouldn't stay standing there. It's 18 parts in total.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
